title: Tohoku-oki fault areas with 20 m or more of USGS-model slip had 0.1-0.3 of their 1998-2011 JMA M3.5+ rate in 2021-2024, and the surrounding 150 km had 1.7 times the old rate
abstract: Question: did the core shutdown and corona activation that Toda and Stein (2022) reported after the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku-oki earthquake continue in 2021-2024, after their data? Does the rate change follow slip from an independent model? Approach: we used the public JMA unified hypocenter catalog for 1998-2024 (M 3.5 or more, depth 70 km or less) and the USGS finite-fault model. We gave each event the slip of the nearest subfault, and we used rings outside a slip-threshold core. We compared post-2011 rates with the 1998-01 to 2011-03-08 rate (30-day block bootstrap, 16 variants of magnitude, depth set and secondary-sequence removal). We also fitted Omori-Utsu decay on days 30-3653 and forecast 2021-03 to 2024-12. Results: where slip was 30 m or more, the rate ratio was 0.36, 0.13 and 0.09 (0.03-0.21) in years 3-5, 5-10 and 10-13.8 (7 events against 74 at the old rate). For all slip of 20 m or more, it was 0.18 (0.10-0.29). In all 16 variants the upper bound was below 1. A decay toward the old rate forecast 75 (54-98) events where slip was 30 m or more. A decay toward a rate near zero fit. The corona (0-150 km) stayed at 1.67 (1.35-2.07) and agreed with the decay forecast (1,641 forecast, 1,553 observed). But deep high slip near the coast (10-20 m) had a ratio of 4.3 (2.2-8.7), from the 2021 Mj 7.3 and 2022 Mj 7.4 intraslab earthquakes. Thus a broad core (slip 13.8 m or more) did not show a shutdown, and the depth of the slip matters. Far-offshore rates north and south did not decrease. Limitations: one slip model, offshore location error, an S-net processing change in 2020, small counts (7-14 events per window), and slip bins added after a first run showed sensitivity to the core definition.

display.caption: Rate ratio to the 1998-01 to 2011-03-08 JMA rate (M 3.5 or more, depth 70 km or less) by the slip of the nearest USGS subfault (left part of each panel) and by distance outside the 13.8 m core (right part), for years 3-5, 5-10 and 10-13.8 after the mainshock. Bars: 95% intervals from a 30-day block bootstrap. Right panel: 30-day secondary sequences of Mj 6 or larger events removed. Dashed line: no change.

Rate ratio on a 0.25-degree grid (M 3.5 or more, depth 70 km or less) for years 5-10 and 10-13.8, relative to 1998-01 to 2011-03-08. Cells need 5 or more events in one of the two periods. Contours: 10, 20 and 30 m slip of the USGS finite-fault model. Coastline: Natural Earth.

Annual M 3.5 or more counts divided by the median annual count of 1998-2010, for three slip bands and the 0-150 km corona. Thin lines: 1998-2010. The 2011 point covers 2011-03-11 to 2011-12-31 as an annual rate. Shaded: years after the Tohoku-oki data of Toda and Stein (2022). Zero counts are drawn at 0.03.

citations.reason: We test the core shutdown and corona activation pattern of this study with 3.8 more years of JMA data and with slip from an independent model. Our results support it for slip of 20 m or more and for the corona.
